title: Head-to-head records — where your score against a friend shows up

steps.headline: Your score against each friend now sits on their row, so you can see it while choosing who to play.
steps.changed: Each friend's row shows how you have done against them AT THIS GAME — your wins first, then theirs, and draws only when there have been some. It is per game on purpose: beating someone at Connect 4 says nothing about who is better at chess, so a combined number would mean nothing. Anyone you have never finished a game against shows no number at all rather than a zero.
steps.measured: 1 line per friend; 0 change for a friend with no record yet
steps.notice: Before you challenge someone you can see whether you are ahead. Early on almost nobody will have a number, so most rows look exactly as they do today.
steps.risk: Seeing that a friend beats you every time could put you off challenging them, which is the opposite of what the arcade is for.

steps.headline: When a match ends, the result card says where that leaves the two of you overall.
steps.changed: One line under the result: You lead 2–0, or Jake leads 3–1, or All square at 4–4. It appears a moment AFTER the result, because the server waits until both players have independently said the same thing about how the game ended before it writes anything down.
steps.measured: 1 line added to a card that already exists; 0 other changes
steps.notice: Winning feels like it counted toward something. If your opponent's app never reports, or the two of you somehow disagree, no line appears and no record is written — the game result itself is unaffected either way.
steps.risk: A quiet gap: if the line does not appear, nothing explains why. Saying more would mean explaining a disagreement most players will never have.
